message.content:
Let \(p=101\). We need

\[
S=\sum_{n=1}^{p-1}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2^{-\lfloor pk/n\rfloor}.
\]

For fixed \(n\), write \(k=tn+s\) with \(t\ge 0\), \(0\le s\le n-1\), excluding \((t,s)=(0,0)\). Then

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{pk}{n}\right\rfloor
=\left\lfloor pt+\frac{ps}{n}\right\rfloor
=pt+\left\lfloor \frac{ps}{n}\right\rfloor.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2^{-\lfloor pk/n\rfloor}
=
\left(\sum_{s=1}^{n-1}2^{-\lfloor ps/n\rfloor}\right)\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}2^{-pt}
+\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}2^{-pt}.
\]

Since \(\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}2^{-pt}=\frac1{1-2^{-p}}\), this becomes

\[
\frac{B_n+2^{-p}}{1-2^{-p}},
\qquad
B_n=\sum_{s=1}^{n-1}2^{-\lfloor ps/n\rfloor}.
\]

Therefore

\[
S=\frac{C+(p-1)2^{-p}}{1-2^{-p}},
\qquad
C=\sum_{n=1}^{p-1}\sum_{s=1}^{n-1}2^{-\lfloor ps/n\rfloor}.
\]

Now evaluate \(C\). For \(1\le s<n\le p-1\), the value \(m=\lfloor ps/n\rfloor\) satisfies \(1\le m\le p-2\). Let \(N_m\) be the number of pairs \((s,n)\) with \(\lfloor ps/n\rfloor=m\). We claim

\[
N_m=\frac{p-1}{2}\qquad (1\le m\le p-2).
\]

For fixed \(m\), let \(r_n\) be the least positive residue of \(-mn\pmod p\). Since \(p\) is prime, \(r_n\in\{1,\dots,p-1\}\). One checks that \(n\) contributes to \(N_m\) exactly when \(r_n<n\): if \(r_n<n\), set

\[
s=\frac{mn+r_n}{p},
\]

which is an integer with \(0<s<n\), and then \(\lfloor ps/n\rfloor=m\). Conversely, if \(\lfloor ps/n\rfloor=m\), writing \(ps=mn+r\) gives \(0<r<n\) and \(r\equiv -mn\pmod p\), so \(r=r_n<n\).

Now let \(a\) be the least positive residue of \(-m\pmod p\). Since \(1\le m\le p-2\), we have \(a\ne 1\). Also,

\[
r_{p-n}\equiv a(p-n)\equiv -an\equiv -r_n\pmod p,
\]

so as positive residues,

\[
r_{p-n}=p-r_n.
\]

Thus \(r_n<n\) if and only if \(r_{p-n}>p-n\). The pairs \(\{n,p-n\}\) partition \(\{1,\dots,p-1\}\), and in each pair exactly one element satisfies the inequality. Hence \(N_m=(p-1)/2\).

Therefore

\[
C=\sum_{m=1}^{p-2}\frac{p-1}{2}2^{-m}
=\frac{p-1}{2}\sum_{m=1}^{p-2}2^{-m}
=\frac{p-1}{2}\left(1-2^{-(p-2)}\right)
=\frac{(p-1)(2^{p-2}-1)}{2^{p-1}}.
\]

Substitute \(p=101\):

\[
C=\frac{100(2^{99}-1)}{2^{100}}.
\]

Then

\[
S=
\frac{\frac{100(2^{99}-1)}{2^{100}}+\frac{100}{2^{101}}}{1-2^{-101}}
=
\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}}
\]
